cuts.reason: Cuts from the wide two-shot (wife walking in with laundry/chips, husband slumped on the couch mid-goal-celebration) straight to both characters collapsed on the floor, hard-cutting past the actual fall to land on the sight gag of him sprawled on top of her body.

Cuts away from the collapsed pair right after 'Hey, hey, are you okay?' to a close-up insert of the soccer match on TV, a beat of misdirection that lets the joke (he's more distracted by the game) breathe before returning to him.
Cuts from the TV insert to a tight close-up on the husband's shocked, frozen face -- a reaction shot that isolates his dawning realization/panic beat in silence before he speaks again.

Cuts back out to the wide floor shot as he repeats 'Are you okay?', re-establishing the full sight gag (him straddling her collapsed body next to the TV) right as the title card 'LOW BATTERY PEOPLE' stamps over the scene, tying the visual punchline to the show's branding.

Cuts from the live-action scene to a black CTA card ('Low Battery People / Created by Nin. / New Episode Daily'), the standard end-slate cut used to close on a branding beat rather than lingering on the joke.

reaction_shots.description: Tight close-up on the husband's face, eyes wide and mouth agape in silent shock/confusion -- a pure reaction shot with no plot action, milking his delayed realization that something is wrong with his wife.

pacing_notes: Shots stay in a fairly tight 1.5-4s band throughout rather than accelerating sharply: the opening wide shot (3.3s) and the collapse shot (3.9s) establish the gag at a relaxed pace, then a quick 1.5s TV insert and a 2.5s silent reaction close-up tighten the rhythm through the joke's beat, before the wide shot returns for the punchline line ('Are you okay?') and lingers for 3.6s while the title card lands. The video then cuts to a single short 1.2s black end card for the CTA, ending on a flat branding beat rather than a fast final cut.
